guarantees.claim: Each control signal in_valid, out_ready, crypt, dec_key_gen, crypt_q, dec_key_gen_q, sub_bytes_out_req, key_expand_out_req is driven directly from a fixed bit of sp2v_sig_chk (bits 0 to 7 respectively).
sp_enc_err is asserted when any bit of sp2v_sig_err is high or sp_enc_err_i is high.
Immediate assertion AesCiphOpValid fires if cfg_valid_i is true and op_i is not CIPH_FWD or CIPH_INV.

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_chk bits accurately represent the respective handshake and control states (in_valid, out_ready, crypt direction, etc.) with no sparsity encoding errors.
assumptions.risk: If sp2v_sig_chk is corrupted, the propagated control signals may cause incorrect cipher operation, data loss, or security bypass.

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_err correctly flags all active sparse encoding errors for the local signals.
assumptions.risk: If sp2v_sig_err fails to assert, sp_enc_err may remain low, hiding a critical encoding fault.

assumptions.claim: sp_enc_err_i reliably aggregates encoding errors from other parts of the cipher core.
assumptions.risk: If sp_enc_err_i is stuck inactive, the global error indication is incomplete, possibly allowing a fault to go unmitigated.

assumptions.claim: cfg_valid_i is only asserted when op_i is stable and valid.
assumptions.risk: If cfg_valid_i asserts while op_i is transitioning, the assertion may fire spuriously or miss a real illegal op_i.

uncertain_points.claim: The correctness of all sp2v_sig_chk-driven signals depends on the sparse encoding checker that produces sp2v_sig_chk and sp2v_sig_err. A bug in that checker would propagate undetected.
uncertain_points.cond: when the sparse encoding checker has a fault
uncertain_points.risk: Functional or security failure due to wrong control signal values.

uncertain_points.claim: sp_enc_err is a combinational error flag; there is no local latching or direct reaction. If the consumer does not promptly halt or reset the cipher, a single-cycle encoding error may lead to corrupted operation.
uncertain_points.risk: Data or key corruption, security leakage if cipher continues after an encoding error.

uncertain_points.claim: The assertion AesCiphOpValid only monitors op_i validity but does not gate cipher operation. An invalid op_i may still reach the cipher datapath, potentially enabling an unforeseen mode.
uncertain_points.cond: when op_i is illegal and assertion fires but cipher is not stopped
uncertain_points.risk: Unknown cipher behavior, possible key/plaintext leakage.
